items.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022
items.q: And I agree with what he said

ctx.x: Well said. I wanted to share something I read recently and this is the first opportunity I’ve had to share it. This is from Kurt Vonnegut from his last book, A Man Without a Country and I’m only slightly paraphrasing here. Kurt said “I really like Strauss and Mozart and all that, but the priceless gift that African-Americans gave the whole world was a gift so great that it is now almost the only reason many foreigners still like us. All pop music today: jazz, swing, bebop, Elvis Presley, the Beatles, the Stones,…

Yeah. It’s the American experience. The blues is the American experience. Now blues didn’t originate in America. Blues came over from Africa. Okay? I don’t know if you’ve had the opportunity or experience to hear some of the, you know, some of the music in Africa that depicts that sound, but it’s there man. I’ve heard it. And the way it developed here is uniqueness. That’s our culture you know. That’s American culture. And I agree with what he said, this is something that has permeated and touched the rest of the…

because we play the music. Okay? I think that’s just something to think about. We are, I don’t know if we’re the only country, modern country, who doesn’t have a Ministry of Culture. Okay? All these Western European countries have a Ministry of Culture where artists are supported. You know? It’s built into their culture. Ours is built-in differently. You know? There’s a whole — I don’t know — do you understand what I’m saying? They have a Ministry of Culture it’s part of the government system. So if an artist —…
